items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: Latin music was very popular so you know the music of Tito Puente, you know, those type of, Eddie Palmieri and everything.

ctx.x: Well junior high school, you know, Motown records were very very popular then so it would be some selection of Motown. And then I grew up in the lower east side of Manhattan and Latin music was very popular so you know the music of Tito Puente, you know, those type of, Eddie Palmieri and everything. I would definitely participate. And then my family is from the Caribbean. My parents came from Montserrat British West Indies, so we always had a lot of calypsos and those types of music from the Caribbean too. So it…
Episcopalian so it wasn’t the Gospel music, but the anthem, the Anglican anthems. We mainly sang those type of things, is the kind of music that my parents listened to.
